sources.situation: the cost-so-far path writes a cache under `.nio/cache/` in the way NFR-2 permits. FR-21 says the `show --json` command writes no file at all. A tester reading FR-21 alone would fail a run that writes a cache, and a reader of NFR-2 cannot tell which rule wins for `show --json`.

findings.title: Context use cannot come from the only source the pane may use
quotes: the pane draws its drill-down from that output only
on Claude Code it is the context window's fill in percent

sources.situation: the host exposes context use (AC-16). The pane must show it. FR-21 limits the pane to the `nio flow show --json` output. AC-23 fixes that output to five keys: timeline, juries, tasks, cost and memory. None of them can hold the session's context fill, which belongs to the host session and not to the effort. The pane either breaks FR-21 or cannot satisfy FR-11 and AC-16.

findings.reason: FR-21 says the pane draws from `flow show --json` only, AC-23 fixes five keys with no context key, yet FR-11 and AC-16 need the host's context fill; no other text names a source.

sources.situation: `nio flow show <slug> --json` runs and the CLI refreshes a cache under `.nio/cache/`. FR-21 says no file is written. NFR-2 allows it. AC-23 checks `git status --porcelain`, which passes only if the cache is ignored. A strict reading of FR-21 fails on the cache write.

findings.title: Cost per stage and per jury is undefined for repeated stages and overlap
quotes: a stage's share being the events between its entry and exit in `history.jsonl`, and a jury's the juror and refuter agents whose run belongs to that gate
findings.fix: define the rule for a re-entered stage, the open stage, and whether jury cost is included in or separate from the stage.

sources.situation: an effort goes back from review to implementing, so a stage is entered twice. Or the effort is still in its current stage, which has an entry and no exit. Or a jury runs inside the spec stage. The spec does not say whether the two entries are summed, whether the open stage counts to now, or whether the jury's tokens are counted again in the stage. AC-12 can then give two different correct totals for the same events.

the effort is unfinished, so its current stage has an entry and no exit, and AC-12 only has finished stages. A test cannot say whether the open stage is counted up to now, left out or shown as `-`. Events outside any entry/exit pair, or a juror whose run belongs to no gate, also have no stated outcome.

findings.reason: FR-7 defines a stage's share as entry-to-exit events only. Nothing says how a re-entered stage, the open stage or jury cost inside a stage is counted, and AC-12 does not fix it.
findings.note: delegated grill Q9: FR-7, AC-12, AC-28 define visits, open stage, unattributed, jury breakdown

sources.situation: the mods are already installed and the human picks skip. The table row says the closing message reads "skipped". The mods are in fact installed. The message gives a false state. FR-18 and the table row `claude | install | yes` treat the installed state, but the skip row ignores it. The state is also undefined when a mod is installed at user scope and not local (FR-25).

findings.note: delegated grill Q10: nio mods install CLI step (FR-29), install ACs on its output and skill text; skip row split by already installed

findings.title: Two features in one spec should be an epic with slices
quotes: This spec adds a drill-down to the
It also makes `@nio:install` on Claude Code install the NIO Claude Code mods
findings.fix: split into an epic with two slices, one for `@nio:install` and the mods (FR-15 to FR-20, FR-22 to FR-26, AC-18 to AC-22, AC-25 to AC-27), one for the drill-down (FR-1 to FR-14, FR-21, AC-1 to AC-17, AC-23, AC-24), with the slice order stated.

sources.situation: one gate jury covers 26 FRs and 27 ACs. If the drill-down's cost figure (FR-7, FR-8, FR-21) fails review, the mod install (FR-15 to FR-26) is blocked with it, although the install needs none of the drill-down code. findings.reason: The Summary ties both parts together as one [human] scope from issue #142, and `epic` is empty by choice. The two parts share no requirement, but the spec as written is a deliberate single spec, not a defect of the text.

findings.title: Local scope install conflicts with the maintainer's "set up once for the team"
quotes: install them for this clone only (Claude Code's `local` scope), changing no file to commit
NIO set up once for the whole team, with hosts, models, budgets and permission prompts chosen for everyone.
findings.fix: state the trade-off in UJ-2 and in the Decisions entry: each clone runs install once, and say which of the two wins. If the team should get the mods once, a committed (project-scope) install is needed, which FR-25 rules out, so the human must choose.

sources.situation: the maintainer runs `@nio:install` once in the repo. A teammate (P-2) clones it and gets no mods, so the pane and the drill-down are missing for them until they run install on their own clone. The persona's "set up once for the whole team" is not met, and the spec does not say so. The intake's goal "nobody has to run ... by hand" is only met per clone.

findings.reason: FR-25 gives local scope per clone, tagged [agent]. A-3 and the persona's "set up once for the team" are not reconciled, and UJ-2 and Decisions state no trade-off.
findings.note: delegated grill Q7: local scope kept, trade-off stated in UJ-2 and Decisions

findings.title: Memory filter in FR-10 is not the one the human asked for, and may not match `nio pack` / `nio query`
quotes: those whose `paths` name a file under the effort's spec folder or whose `against` names the effort
Observable: the listed IDs equal those `nio pack` / `nio query` return for the effort.
findings.fix: either make FR-10 say "the records `nio pack` returns for the effort" (and read them without the embedding model if that is possible), or retag FR-10 as [default] and state the filter rule as a decision the grill must confirm.

sources.situation: a decision record about `src/nio/pack.py`, with no `paths` entry under the spec folder and no `against` naming the effort, is returned by `nio pack` for this effort but is not listed in the drill-down. AC-15 then fails although FR-10 was built as written. The reverse can also happen. FR-10 is tagged [human], but the human's words only name `nio pack` / `nio query` as the source.

`nio pack` and `nio query` rank by relevance and use the embedding model, while FR-10 selects by `paths` and `against` from the front matter. A record that matches by `paths` but is not returned by `nio query` makes the AC-15 test fail although FR-10 holds. A query hit that has neither `paths` nor `against` makes AC-15 pass although FR-10 is broken. The AC doesn't test the FR.

findings.reason: FR-10 filters on `paths` and `against` front matter, while AC-15's observable is equality with `nio pack` / `nio query`, which rank by relevance. The two sets can differ, so the AC does not test the FR.
findings.note: delegated grill Q8: front-matter filter kept, FR-10 retagged agent, AC-15 checks the filter

findings.title: "Failed review" is never defined
quotes: WHEN the effort's history holds a failed review THE SYSTEM SHALL show it in the timeline with its reason.
Given a history with a failed review
findings.fix: name the history field and value that mark a failed review, and give the output when the reason is missing.

sources.situation: the spec doesn't say which `history.jsonl` entry is a failed review: a field value, an event kind, or a stage change back. A test author must guess the fixture, and one reading shows a review that another reading treats as an ordinary stage change. A failed review with no recorded reason is also uncovered.

findings.reason: FR-3 and AC-2 never name the `history.jsonl` field or value that marks a failed review, and the output when the reason is missing is not given.

findings.title: Install ACs observe an agent transcript, not a deterministic output
quotes: no mod question in the transcript
the skill asks exactly one question about the mods
findings.fix: say how each is checked, either as a fixed script or CLI step that is unit-tested, or as an e2e with a recorded tolerance. Or move the question count out of the AC.

sources.situation: `@nio:install` is a markdown skill that a model follows, and these ACs are marked `integration`. "Exactly one question" and "no question" depend on model behaviour, so a run can pass once and fail the next with no code change. No harness or fixture is named that makes it repeatable. The same applies to "the closing message holds the mod's name and error" in AC-21.

findings.reason: AC-22 and AC-26 observe "the transcript" and the number of questions the markdown skill asks, with level integration and no harness named. This depends on model behaviour and is not repeatable.
findings.note: delegated grill Q10: nio mods install CLI step (FR-29), install ACs on its output and skill text; skip row split by already installed

findings.title: `nio flow show` has no failure case
quotes: WHEN asked with `nio flow show <slug> --json` THE SYSTEM SHALL print, as one JSON object
findings.fix: add an AC for an unknown or finished slug that fixes the exit code and the JSON error shape, and one for the pane showing it.

sources.situation: nothing says what the command prints, or its exit code, for an unknown slug, a finished effort (the cost is for unfinished efforts only), or an effort that finishes between the pane list and the selection.
